findings: The complete guide covers ordering, a cancelable Pending state lasting at least 30 minutes, Ready to ship with cancellation closed, and Shipped when tracking is available. It also identifies Canceled, Delivered and Undeliverable.

The optional Hardware Orders API preview step validates and estimates taxes without creation. Country-matched available SKUs and shipping methods must share a provider; account manager, monthly invoice billing and sales eligibility assessment apply to preview access.

Dashboard returns require eligible shipped or delivered Dashboard orders in supported countries and user permission. The package must include original packaging and accessories within 30 days, the first initiated return refunds shipping fees, and receipt at the distribution facility triggers the refund, with credit card funds taking up to 10 days.
substantive_changes: The November guide adds order-time preregistration of eligible smart readers. One selected Terminal location per order can be changed on the details page until serial numbers are available. Stripe then automatically registers eligible readers. For multiple locations, wait for serial numbers and register readers individually by serial number.

For accounts with Hardware Orders API preview access, Stripe can emit registered or registration_failed per-device outcomes following automatic attempts. The event data.object is a Hardware Order Device, which can be correlated by device ID, serial number and hardware order relationship. These are additions alongside six order-level events.
The documented Stripe-Version header changes from 2026-04-22.dahlia to 2026-10-28.endive while terminal_hardware_orders_beta stays v5, including the webhook endpoint version guidance.

The 2026-11-07 self-service list has 32 entries versus 33 in May. GI is no longer listed for self-service but remains in the distinct shipping table. The November fallback for unsupported self-service countries is contacting Support through the Dashboard order.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the full 2026-05-01 capture, six order-state webhooks and earlier version pairing as dated evidence. Keep historical v3/v4 same-mode duplicate shipped-event warning and v3/v4 status mapping without generalizing to v5.

Preserve Dashboard permissions, cutoff and signature thresholds by shipping destination, shipping/returns distinction, 30-day fallback guidance, and sandbox-only status helpers. The cap is 10,000 of each item in a single order in both captures.
Keep existing manual registration methods as separate routes from November order-time automation, and preserve the original packaging, accessories and first-return shipping-fee qualifications.
conflicts: The mapped source, provider index, company page and Terminal hardware concepts retain an undated 33-country return count or GI listing. Date that prior fact and route the current summary to the November 32-entry list without inferring the shipping table changed.

The mapped source and wiki/concepts/stripe-terminal-hardware-orders.md:59-70 retain the May header and order-only event inventory as the undated picture. Date the earlier pairing and six order events, and add November's preview-dependent device events.

The mapped source and both Terminal hardware concepts say 10,000 units per order. Both captures say up to 10,000 of each item per single order. The mapped introduction and dedicated concept also conflate API ordering with Dashboard returns. Separate those paths; the guide establishes Dashboard return steps, including the support fallback.

The mapped raw link implies 37 destinations in the shipping table. Both tables have 40 destination rows; remove or correct the count. The broad fleet concept's ship-to-any-location wording needs the documented destination and physical-address qualifications.
unresolved_questions: The 2026-11-07 capture omits GI from the self-service list but does not give the operational effective date or account-specific eligibility. The capture does not enumerate all preregistration-eligible smart-reader models.

findings: Add the dated November order-time preregistration, location/serial boundaries, beta header and distinct device outcomes, and update the dated self-service return scope while retaining the prior raw.
conflicts: Correct per-item cap and shipping-table count, separate API order creation from documented Dashboard return workflow and preserve reciprocal concept and company/index routes.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/fleet/order-and-return-readers, source-stripe-terminal-order-and-return-readers documents Dashboard purchase of pre-certified hardware and the account-manager and monthly-invoice-gated Hardware Orders API preview. Pending orders are cancelable in the Dashboard and remain pending at least 30 minutes. Ready to ship ends cancellation, tracking advances the order to Shipped, and the November diagram shows Pending also branching to Canceled and Shipped branching to Delivered or Undeliverable (old raw lines 26-39 and new raw lines 27-48). The preview API retrieves compatible country/provider SKUs and shipping methods before optional validation without creation and then creation (old raw lines 194-216 and old raw lines 238-264 and old raw lines 286-292, new raw lines 212-234 and new raw lines 256-282 and new raw lines 304-310). November adds selecting one editable Terminal location per order until serial numbers appear. Stripe then automatically registers eligible smart readers, with individual serial registration for orders split across locations and preview-access-dependent per-device outcomes (old raw lines 39-45 and old raw lines 335-344, new raw lines 50-58 and new raw lines 353-364). Self-service is a Dashboard workflow with permission, eligible Shipped or Delivered orders and qualifying original packaging/accessories within 30 days. A received package triggers refund and shipping fees are refunded on the first initiated return (old raw lines 41-49 and old raw lines 87-101, new raw lines 60-68 and new raw lines 105-119). Its list is smaller in November. The current summary covers the lifecycle and historical preview workflow but omits preregistration and still gives the May header, six-event inventory, 33-country return count and an incorrect order-wide quantity limit (old raw lines 19-20 and new raw lines 20-21).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/fleet/order-and-return-readers, update source-stripe-terminal-order-and-return-readers. The latter concern automatic attempts on eligible devices and use the Hardware Order Device payload, rather than an order-wide outcome (old raw line 216 and old raw lines 335-344, new raw lines 50-58 and new raw line 234 and new raw lines 353-364).
